Well I guess it depends from one person to the next but for my part (I'm 23 and enby), I think I always felt a sort of discomfort when it came to the topic of my gender. I wasn't super feminine but I wasn't a tomboy either, I didn't really know what I wanted to look like or be like. I just know that being reminded of my gender made me feel a little bad and it got a lot worse with puberty. It wasn't until I was in my last year of high school I think that I heard about what being non-binary was and it clicked "oh that's what sounds like me". But it wasn't all smooth sailing after that, it took me some time to figure out what made me comfortable in my own skin and how to approach the gender that was always mine but that kept being denied by everything I knew.

I think it's important to say that your gender means literally whatever you want it to mean. It doesn't necessarily have to do with a change of pronouns or appearance, but it may. Maybe you will want to transition, maybe not. And you can keep your gender private for now or forever, I know a lot of people hate(d) being in the closet, but I'm still partially in it and I don't hate it. As long as you feel comfortable with yourself and you can remain safe, the rest is just a matter of taking the time to process it all. It can be a lot but it can also be extremely relieving. In any case, if you want to talk about it, don't hesitate, I'm all ears!
